title: Cross-validation repeats a check
summary: Cross-validation trains and evaluates on several train/validation splits. It gives more than one estimate, but still needs careful data grouping.
introduction: Cross-validation trains and evaluates on several train/validation splits. It gives more than one estimate, but still needs careful data grouping. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Cross-validation trains and evaluates on several train/validation splits. It gives more than one estimate, but still needs careful data grouping.

blocks.code:
from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeClassifier
from sklearn.model_selection import cross_val_score
X, y = load_iris(return_X_y=True)
scores = cross_val_score(DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth=2, random_state=0), X, y, cv=3)
print(len(scores))
blocks.title: Cross-validation repeats a check

blocks.text: The output is 3 because three validation folds were used. Iris is included with scikit-learn; no download is needed.
